name: Crosshair-TS-TW

frames.best_why: Frame 3 catches the glitch, with the horizontal guide rippling across the panel.

tagline: Fine white crosshair lines track the pointer across the page.
summary: Two hairline white guides follow the mouse across a dark editorial panel, and they shudder with a noise glitch whenever the pointer touches a link.
appearance: A near-black panel with a small letterspaced kicker, a heavy white headline, a line of grey copy and two underlined links. A one-pixel white horizontal and vertical line intersect where the pointer is, spanning the panel.
behaviour: The two guide lines trail the pointer with a slight lag and fade in once the mouse enters. Hovering either link shakes both lines with a turbulence filter for half a second, then lets them settle.
demo_content: Kicker "Field notes, vol. 04", headline "Aim small, miss small.", two links.
search_phrases: thin guide lines following the mouse pointer
horizontal and vertical lines tracking cursor
noise jitter when hovering a link
use_when: An editorial or portfolio page wants a precise aiming reticle instead of a normal pointer.
avoid_when: It needs a mouse to appear, and the page must hide the real cursor or the two will overlap.
customise: Line colour and the container to track are props; the glitch filter, the 0.15 follow lag and the line thickness are fixed in the source.
weight_why: Two one-pixel divs moved each frame, with a short SVG turbulence glitch on hover.

a11y.note: The guides only exist for a mouse; they vanish for keyboard users and there is no reduced-motion handling.

issues: The crosshair does nothing for keyboard users and hides when the pointer leaves the container.
If the page does not hide the native cursor, both pointers show at once.
polish_why: Sharp editorial composition and a restrained glitch; the guides can cross the headline awkwardly.
